text.content: CWAM B5 VOM R8 high-utilization B128 probe

Determine whether disabling activation checkpointing and increasing micro-batch from 64 to 128 per rank improves sustained sample throughput and B200 memory utilization without OOM, nonfinite gradients, or loss of aligned-memory intervention dependence.

Complete 100 finite optimizer steps on 8 B200s; no OOM, traceback, NCCL, or nonfinite gradients; peak memory below 90%; steady-state throughput above the R7 baseline of about 160 samples/s; final matched validation aligned action loss at least 1% below both exact-zero and shuffled memory.
88f3c95c18a3f3195b66e35b2cd8f6ecfe595b81 training source; 1fe84a6 high-utilization launcher and iteration record (pushed)

R4 step-500 model-only warm start; optimizer/scheduler/trainer restart at zero; R6-A dynamic-exclusive full final-delta architecture; R7 aligned/zero/shuffle policy ranking weight=1.0, relative margin=1%, warmup=50; 100 steps; batch 128/rank, DP8, global 1024; token cap 296000; activation checkpointing none; validation at step 0 and 100; checkpoint at 100.
RoboCasa365 B4 processed split plus 1,143,698-record triple-view Wan latent cache and episode-safe t-36/t-24/t-12 visual-history sidecar; same stream and data contract as R7; no future lookup.
pyrogpucompute1; 8 x NVIDIA B200 183359 MiB; batch 128/rank; effective global batch 1024.
Steady-state seconds/step and samples/s; GPU utilization, peak memory, and power; finite/nonzero action gradients; aligned/zero/shuffle action losses and relative gains; checkpoint completeness.

This probe is isolated from the underutilized R7 formal run. It starts from the same R4 model-only checkpoint, uses a fresh optimizer and scheduler, and writes to a new run root. The selected formal configuration must maximize stable sample throughput while retaining the preregistered causal intervention gate; memory occupancy alone is not sufficient.
